# Registry content for Microsoft's storage stack on QEMU's q35 machine,
# laid over the SYSTEM hive with registry-overlay.txt in the boots that
# ask for it (a scenario's `registry = "storage"`; tools/mkesp.py).
#
# Every value is copied from the reference Windows 10 installation
# (10.0.19045.2006, the same machine type, its system disk on the ICH9
# AHCI controller): the service keys of acpi.sys, pci.sys, storahci.sys
# and disk.sys and of the filters Windows puts in the disk's stack, the
# device classes, the driver database records that match the device IDs
# of the path to their drivers, the Control keys these drivers read, and
# the two root device keys from which enumeration starts. Letter case is
# as found. Windows keeps DriverDatabase in a hive of its own, mounted
# at this path.
#
# Not here, on purpose: the Enum keys the Plug and Play manager makes
# for the devices it enumerates, each service's volatile Enum subkey,
# and the Class\{guid}\NNNN driver keys made when a device is installed.
#
# Like registry-overlay.txt, this belongs in the Windows-written hive
# and moves there at the next release of the fixtures.

# --- Services --------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Of the seven binaries only acpi.sys, pci.sys, storahci.sys and disk.sys are
# services. storport.sys, classpnp.sys and pshed.dll have NO Services key: they are
# loaded as imports (storahci -> storport, disk -> classpnp, the kernel -> pshed).
# ImagePath is relative to \SystemRoot. All are Type 1, Start 0 (boot).
# Each key also has a volatile subkey Enum (Count, NextInstance, 0 = instance id)
# that the PnP manager writes when it starts a device with the service.

# Group is "Core": that name is NOT in ServiceGroupOrder\List and has no line in
# GroupOrderList, yet ACPI.sys is among the first drivers the boot log shows.
# ErrorControl 3 (critical). acpi.inf sets Tag and Group by AddReg and creates no
# Parameters values: the four below are not in the INF, so they were written at
# run time (by acpi.sys / its WPP recorder). The binaries are 4 zero bytes each.
key ControlSet001\Services\ACPI
value ImagePath expand_sz System32\drivers\ACPI.sys
value Type dword 1
value Start dword 0
value ErrorControl dword 3
value DisplayName sz "@acpi.inf,%ACPI.SvcDesc%;Microsoft ACPI Driver"
value Owners multi_sz acpi.inf
value Tag dword 2
value Group sz Core
key ControlSet001\Services\ACPI\Parameters
value WHEAOSCImplemented binary hex:00000000
value APEIOSCGranted binary hex:00000000
value CPPCRevisionGranted binary hex:00000000
value WppRecorder_TraceGuid sz {03906a40-cce8-447f-83f4-e2346215db84}

key ControlSet001\Services\pci
value ImagePath expand_sz System32\drivers\pci.sys
value Type dword 1
value Start dword 0
value ErrorControl dword 3
value Group sz "Boot Bus Extender"
value Tag dword 3
value DisplayName sz "@pci.inf,%pci_svcdesc%;PCI Bus Driver"
value Owners multi_sz pci.inf machine.inf pcmcia.inf
key ControlSet001\Services\pci\Parameters
value DmaRemappingCompatible dword 1
value WppRecorder_TraceGuid sz {47711976-08c7-44ef-8fa2-082da6a30a30}

# Group is spelled "SCSI Miniport" here and "SCSI miniport" in ServiceGroupOrder.

# --- Device id -> driver matching -------------------------------------------------
#
# This build has NO Control\CriticalDeviceDatabase key. Matching data is the driver
# database: HKLM\SYSTEM\DriverDatabase, which on Windows is a separate hive
# (\SystemRoot\System32\config\DRIVERS, mounted as \Registry\Machine\DRIVERS;
# SYSTEM\DriverDatabase is how it is reached). Paths below are written as if it
# were a key of the SYSTEM hive: NK decides where it lives.
#   DeviceIds\<id>: value <inf name> = 01 ff 00 00 -> which INF matches the id
#   DriverInfFiles\<inf>: Active -> the package key
#   DriverPackages\<pkg>\Descriptors\<id>: Configuration -> the install section
#   DriverPackages\<pkg>\Configurations\<section>: Service, and the registry
#      content the section adds (Device\... -> the device's "Device Parameters",
#      Services\... -> the service key)
# Only the ids and sections of this device path are copied. Windows stores some
# values there with types outside the standard set (0x40007 = multi_sz with a flag
# in the high word; 0xffff00NN = a DEVPROP type): the format cannot express them,
# so they are comments with their data.
# UpdateDate is a FILETIME of this installation.
key DriverDatabase
value Version dword 0xa000000
value SchemaVersion dword 0x10000
value Architecture dword 9
value UpdateDate binary hex:c0b7943d31c3d801
value SetupStatus dword 0
value OemInfMap binary hex:c0

# --- Control keys the drivers read ------------------------------------------------
#
# ABSENT on Windows (the drivers get STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND; do not create):
#   Control\CriticalDeviceDatabase, Control\DISK, Control\Classpnp, Control\WHEA,
#   Control\Processor, Control\BiosInfo (so no BiosInfo\PCI), Control\MiniNT.

# acpi and pci: arbiter configuration. All values are resource requirements lists
# or the name of another value of the same key.

value Root resource_requirements_list hex:

# What starts ACPI. The device is REPORTED, not installed from the registry: the HAL
# calls IoReportDetectedDevice at boot (DeviceReported = 1, compatible ids
# DETECTEDInternal\ACPI_HAL and DETECTED\ACPI_HAL), its driver is the HAL's own
# driver object \Driver\ACPI_HAL (there is no Services\ACPI_HAL key), and that
# driver enumerates the one child ACPI_HAL\PNP0C08\0, which acpi.inf gives to
# service ACPI. This key is what the report leaves behind; ClassGUID, DeviceDesc,
# Driver and Mfg name hal.inf, so device installation added them. Its Properties
# subkeys (DEVPROP-typed values) are not copied. Control is a volatile subkey.
key ControlSet001\Enum\ROOT\ACPI_HAL\0000
value ConfigFlags dword 0
value DeviceReported dword 1
value Service sz \Driver\ACPI_HAL
value CompatibleIDs multi_sz DETECTEDInternal\ACPI_HAL DETECTED\ACPI_HAL
value HardwareID multi_sz acpiapic
value ClassGUID sz {4d36e966-e325-11ce-bfc1-08002be10318}
value DeviceDesc sz "@hal.inf,%acpi_amd64.devicedesc%;ACPI x64-based PC"
value Driver sz {4d36e966-e325-11ce-bfc1-08002be10318}\0000
value Mfg sz "@hal.inf,%gendev_mfg%;(Standard computers)"
value ContainerID sz {00000000-0000-0000-FFFF-FFFFFFFFFFFF}
value Capabilities dword 0
